## Separate Two Speakers (MossFormer2)

Two people talking over each other, split into one track each: `output/audio/speaker_1_...` and
`speaker_2_...`. Listen and keep the one you need; which speaker lands on track 1 depends on the recording.
Use it before subtitles or speech to text, or to get a clean reference voice for cloning.

**Separate Two Speakers** runs MossFormer2_SS_16K from Alibaba's ClearerVoice-Studio (Apache-2.0). The model
was trained on short mixtures, so the node works in 20 s windows that overlap by 4 s, keeps each speaker on the
same track from window to window, and crossfades. The output is 16 kHz, mono.

Measured on 3 minutes of Finnish read speech with an English speaker over it at the same level: the Finnish
voice stayed on one track throughout; Nemotron's character errors fell from 74 % to 27 % and Whisper's from 82 %
to 22 % (on the clean speech: 6 % and 3 %). Not for three or more voices at once: with four people talking
behind the speaker it did not help. For noise, music and room sound use Clean Up Voice (Inworld Voice Isolator);
do not chain the two: the isolator after this node made the errors worse (29 % and 31 %).

## Settings worth knowing

- **window_seconds**: 20, the best in the test; the whole file at once came out much worse.
- **overlap_seconds**: 4; used to match the speakers between windows.
- 3 minutes take about half a minute.

## Model

`models/speech_separation/mossformer2_ss_16k.pt` (0.67 GB), `last_best_checkpoint.pt` of
[alibabasglab/MossFormer2_SS_16K](https://huggingface.co/alibabasglab/MossFormer2_SS_16K), renamed. The node
downloads it on first use (pinned, sha256 checked) and loads it as plain data. Profile `speech-separation`.

## Where this workflow comes from

Our own graph. The model code is vendored from ClearerVoice-Studio (pack `vendor/mossformer2_ss/`, licence in
`licenses/`). The sample mixes a FLEURS Finnish sentence recording (Google, CC BY 4.0) with a LibriVox reading
(public domain).
